transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-07 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Kim (CTO, Sable), Raj Patel (Head of ML), Maya Ortiz (Platform), Oliver Chen (Procurement)

---
Summary (auto): quick discovery focused on Dedicated reserve + hot-pool prewarm for bursty drug-design workloads. Discussed isolation needs, prewarming strategies, and cost/latency tradeoffs.

Topics: reserved pool sizing, hot-pool pre-warming, preemption tolerance, KV cache / prefix caching, KMS & audit logs, pilot run.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samantha: Hey all, thanks for joining, this is Samantha from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Marco from engineering is with me. How's everyone's afternoon?
[00:08] Dr. Lena Kim: Hi — good thanks, excited to dig in. Quick context: we run generative pipelines for molecule enumeration, very latency sensitive for editor workflow, plus nightly batched scoring.
[00:20] Marco: Great, can you give us a sense of what "latency sensitive" means — p95 goals, token sizes, seq len?
[00:27] Raj: Sure. For the interactive editor we want p95 under 500ms for 256 token prompts typical, occasionally 1024 for longer reranks. Throughput is low for interactive (10–60 qps) but scoring jobs spike — like 400 concurrent token streams for 10–15 minutes.
[00:44] Samantha: Good — so sounds like baseline dedicated capacity with a burst mechanism makes sense. Do you already use cloud GPUs or self-host?
[00:51] Maya: We're hybrid. Prod inference is on GKE with node pools, but it's noisy neighbors on shared clusters. That's why we're exploring full tenancy.
[01:01] Oliver: From procurement, we need predictable monthly commitments but also headroom for spikes — otherwise the manual scaling is painful.
[01:08] Marco: Understood. Two main options we see: fully isolated reserved capacity (hard tenancy) sized to baseline, plus a hot prewarmed pool that can attach to your VPC briefly for bursts; or a larger reserved pool and autoscale inside it. Hot-pool helps control idle costs.
[01:25] Raj: Can you explain "hot prewarmed"? Is that like VM-level warm or GPU kernel warm?
[01:29] Marco: It's both — we keep nodes with the model already loaded and KV cache populated for expected prefixes; cold start is mostly model load and CUDA kernel JIT in some stacks. Prewarmed nodes reduce first-token latency from seconds to sub-500ms. There is a tradeoff: prewarm costs money but saves latency.
[01:46] Raj: Hmm, and what's the preemption behavior if we need dedicated isolation? We can't have other tenants on those nodes.
[01:52] Samantha: For Dedicated we offer options — hard tenancy (node-level isolation) or soft tenancy (capped multi-tenant). For Sable's compliance concerns you probably want hard tenancy. The hot pool can be dedicated nodes that are kept warm but not assigned until burst.
[02:07] Dr. Lena Kim: Our security team also needs KMS/HSM support for model keys and ability to rotate keys. Can Redwood integrate with our KMS?
[02:15] Marco: Yes, Private and Dedicated both support customer-managed KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Cloud HSM patterns). We'll capture the exact provider in the follow-up.
[02:22] Maya: Also need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM and SSO via SAML.
[02:26] Samantha: Standard — we have SOC2 reports and SAML SSO integrations; we'll share the security packet after this call.
[02:33] Oliver: Pricing? We need a monthly commit but with some burst credits for prewarmed capacity usage. Any patterns you've seen?
[02:41] Marco: We often model base reserved capacity for 70–80% of usual baseline, and sell burst credits or prewarmed minute buckets for the rest. For example, a customer reserves 8 A100-equivalent GPUs for steady state and wastes less by using a prewarm pool that charges per-minute while in hot state.
[03:00] Raj: How do you measure the per-minute billing for prewarmed nodes? If a spike hits for 12 minutes are we billed full hour?
[03:07] Samantha: We have minute-granular billing on the hot pool; but reserved capacity is billed by the commit term. There are also burst-credit pools you can buy at a discount.
[03:16] Raj: Nice. Do you support node preemption or graceful draining? We need sessions to failover to fallback model if preempted.
[03:24] Marco: Yes — we have automatic fallback policies. If a hot node can't attach we route to an alternate smaller model (quantized variant) or queued tokens with a short timeout. We can tune that per route.
[03:36] Dr. Lena Kim: Our workloads include long KV-cache heavy sessions for RLHF sampling sometimes, will that be impacted by swapping nodes?
[03:43] Marco: KV cache migration is tricky mid-session; we recommend sticky assignment for long-running sessions and try to avoid preemption mid-stream. Prewarmed nodes can be reserved for sticky sessions to guarantee KV locality.
[03:54] Raj: On model compatibility: we use a mix of LLaMA derivatives and a private transformer with custom layers. Can Redwood host custom models in Dedicated?
[04:03] Marco: Yes — we onboard customer model artifacts in Dedicated and Private; sometimes custom ops require a brief compatibility shim. We'll need access to the model wheel/tar and ideally a small test container.
[04:15] Raj: Ok we'll provide a sample artifact for the benchmark.
[04:19] Samantha: Speaking of benchmarks, would you be open to a 2-hour perf run where we run your model on an isolated node to measure cold vs warm p95/p99?
[04:27] Dr. Lena Kim: Yes, that's useful. We want numbers to feed procurement.
[04:31] Marco: For the benchmark we'll need: model artifact, representative prompt set and token length distribution, and traffic shape (burst size and duration). Also clarify success criteria: say p95 < 500ms for interactive and p99 < 1.2s, or similar.
[04:44] Raj: We'll share histograms but can we also test the prewarm pool transitions — like attach/detach time and the p95 degradation when burned through initial warm nodes?
[04:53] Marco: Absolutely. We'll simulate the burst: baseline traffic then a 10–15 minute spike to replicate your scoring jobs and measure attach latency and queue tail behavior.
[05:04] Maya: Network and VPC: how does the hot pool attach to our VPC? Any NAT/EIP constraints?
[05:09] Marco: Hot nodes will be provisioned in your VPC via peering or private link; we can use secondary subnets and route tables. Egress policies follow your VPC rules. There is a short attach handshake to establish routing; we'll document the exact ports and IP whitelists.
[05:23] Oliver: Procurement question — what contract terms exist around reserved capacity upgrades if we under/overestimate?
[05:29] Samantha: We offer quarterly reassessment windows for resizing and options to purchase additional burst minutes. There are standard change-order processes for bigger capacity moves.
[05:37] Raj: Any limitations on per-tenant GPU types? We prefer A100s today but are curious about L40s or lower-cost q8 variant nodes.
[05:45] Marco: We can provision different GPU classes in Dedicated; cost/latency vary. We recommend A100/NVIDIA H100 for heavy dense models. For cost-sensitive paths we can recommend quantized variants on cheaper GPUs.
[05:56] Dr. Lena Kim: One subtlety — our models use a custom HPM op that does some fused attention. Will Redwood allow kernel uploads or custom ops?
[06:03] Marco: We can support custom ops but need to review them in our security/ops process. In Dedicated/Private we have more leeway; we'll ask for the repo and a small unit test. Might require a brief compatibility shim.
[06:15] Raj: Great. Any pitfalls you've seen with similar customers?
[06:19] Marco: Biggest surprises: underestimating burst tail (customers hit a sudden long tail), and neglecting cache warmups for common prefixes which made cold p95 much worse. Also network egress throttles when a whole pool drains to downstream services.
[06:34] Samantha: Ok let's recap: Sable will share token histograms, model artifacts, and security contact. Redwood will send pricing with reserved + hot-pool options, a proposed benchmark plan, and required VPC/KMS docs. We'll aim for a pilot week of 2026-10-20.
[06:49] Dr. Lena Kim: Sounds good. I also want to loop in our security lead on the next call.
[06:54] Oliver: From procurement we'll review pricing once we get the concrete numbers.
[06:57] Samantha: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet.
[07:01] (call wraps)

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms — "K V cash" for KV cache, and speaker labeling may shift in the middle when multiple folks talk over each other.

End of transcript
